name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It catches routing errors after they’ve already shipped, so we see real-world failures without risking new ones. The trade-off is delayed feedback on open PRs, but merged PRs are where fixes matter most. This is the fastest way to harden our self-improvement loop.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs only catches errors *after* they’re already in product—it doesn’t prevent them. The real risk is normalizing shipping broken routing and treating fixes as cleanup, not prevention. A better alternative is running PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first; it catches errors before they ship, and we can still run merged PRs in shadow to catch regressions. Settle it by testing both: run shadow mode on open PRs for two weeks, measure error rates in merged PRs, and compare.
